by Neptune, one the **Solar Tree** <note>original: *Solaris Arbor*</note>, and the other the **Lunar Tree** <note>original: *Lunaris*</note>. And although everything in this island was available at a whim, yet one single thing was lacking. Water was not to be had, except with great difficulty. There were indeed many who attempted in part to lead spring water <note>original: *Aqua Fontis*</note> there through channels; and in part they even extracted it from various things. But the attempted labor was in vain, because in those places it could be obtained by no means. Even if it was obtained, it was nevertheless useless and poisonous, unless it was drawn from the rays of the **Sun** or the **Moon** <note>The "water" of the alchemists is often described as a celestial "dew" or "spirit" captured from the air or light, rather than common water.</note>, which few were able to provide; and whoever had a favorable fortune in accomplishing this, could never attract more than ten parts. For water of this kind was miraculous; and believe me, that I saw with my own eyes and touched with my hands the snowy whiteness of that water, and while I contemplated that water, I was greatly changed. 

Meanwhile, fatigued by that contemplation, **Neptune** vanished from before my eyes, and there appeared to me a great man, upon whose forehead the name of **Saturn** was inscribed. He, having taken a vessel, drew up ten parts of the water, and immediately from the fru- <note>The text continues as *fructibus* (fruits) on the following page.</note>

<summary>The narrator describes the difficulty of obtaining the miraculous "water" of the island, which must be drawn from celestial rays, before meeting the figure of Saturn.</summary>
<keywords>Solar Tree, Lunar Tree, alchemical water, Sun, Moon, Neptune, Saturn, allegory</keywords>
